notes: B1 and the overlay grammar. research-builtin.yml is a golden copy of the shipped built-in research workflow: the suite resolves it and the shipped definition and asserts one graph_hash for both, so a drift in either turns the suite red. It warns about nothing at all, which makes its expected warning set empty and any new warning a regression; research-builtin.md is the prose companion its direct: nodes resolve against, since a companion is looked for beside the file that declares the node. development-builtin.yml is the same arrangement for the shipped built-in development workflow, asserted to one graph_hash with it and carrying development-builtin.md as its companion; its golden hash lives in the suite source, because expect is closed and a hash is not part of its vocabulary. plan-builtin.yml is the same arrangement again for the shipped built-in plan workflow - the chain-only definition that has no orchestrator skill and no slash command - asserted to one graph_hash with it and carrying plan-builtin.md as its companion; its golden hash lives in the suite source for the same reason. richtext is the launch chain (a gate node with exactly one continue and two stop options, a when guard in the negated form, dir/provider per node, on: always on the close-out). overlay.yml exercises extends/add/tune/disable/profiles against builtin:development, and is resolved against it rather than only validated standalone. It was written against node ids the base does not declare - implement, verify, generate-mockups, audit-spec, where the base says implementation, verification, ui-mockups and spec-audit - and it added a node whose uses named a command rather than a skill and tuned a provider onto a node with no dir. Standalone validation resolves no references and never applies an overlay to a base, so nothing in the repository could reach any of it, and a shipped fixture is what a reader copies. reserved-keys.yml carries all eight R keys and is the source of expect.warnings; version-99.yml carries version 99 plus unknown node and root keys and is the source of expect.degraded. Both are valid: unknown version degrades, it never errors. version-99.yml carries schema null on purpose: a document that declares a newer format cannot validate against the v1 const, and the expectation is the runner reporting degraded: newer-format rather than a schema pass.
